headlines.title: NextEra Energy (NEE) Has Bigger Growth Ambitions. Is Duke Energy (DUK) the Better Buy?
headlines.summary: NextEra Energy, Inc. (NYSE:NEE) and Duke Energy Corporation (NYSE:DUK) have returned -13.29% and -6.77%, respectively, over the last six months, as of October 15. This compares to a 21.5% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 15.74% for the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.

headlines.title: Did NextEra's Dividends Make Up For Its Stock's Lag Behind The Market?
headlines.summary: NextEra Energy (NEE) sells electricity primarily through its Florida utility and pays a dividend yielding 3.0% at the October 15, 2026 close. Investors holding the stock are likely doing so for that regular cash payout. The company's share price has lagged the broader market over the past five years. So, once every dividend is counted, what would you guess a holder ended up with over five years, next to the market.

headlines.title: NEE Stock Falls Behind Industry in 3 Months: Should You Buy Now?
headlines.summary: NextEra Energy's shares fall 10.5% in three months. Strong clean energy demand and rising earnings estimates support growth, but its premium valuation is a concern.

headlines.title: NextEra’s $4M Trump ballroom donation muddies Dominion merger debate, watchdogs say
headlines.summary: The donation, which advocates called “problematic” and “convenient” for the company, comes to light as federal regulators chosen by President Donald Trump consider whether to allow NextEra to merge with Dominion Energy.

headlines.title: NextEra Energy (NEE) Faces Uncertainty Over Its Proposed $67 Billion Acquisition
headlines.summary: Guinness Global Investors recently released its “Guinness Sustainable Energy Fund” Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here. The fund faced a challenging third-quarter 2026 investment environment as rising interest rates, persistent inflation, and a rotation away from growth stocks weighed on renewable-energy and electrification shares. The Fund declined 8.

description: NextEra Energy, Inc., through its subsidiaries, generates, stores, transmits, distributes, and sells electric power to retail and wholesale customers in North America. It operates through Florida Power & Light Company (FPL) and NEER segments. The company generates electricity from wind, solar, nuclear, natural gas, and other clean energy assets. It also invests in generation, storage, transmission, and distribution facilities; owns, develops, constructs, manages, and operates generation facilities, including renewables, nuclear and natural gas, and battery storage facilities in the wholesale energy market in the United States and Canada, as well as electric and gas transmission assets, and natural gas pipelines; provides full energy and capacity requirement services; markets and trades in energy-related commodities; and participates in the production of natural gas, natural gas liquids, and oil. As of December 31, 2025, the company had approximately 35,963 megawatts of net generating capacity; approximately 93,000 circuit miles of transmission and distribution lines; and 932 substations. It serves approximately 12 million people through approximately 6 million customer accounts on the east and lower west coasts of Florida. The company was formerly known as FPL Group, Inc. and changed its name to NextEra Energy, Inc. in 2010. NextEra Energy, Inc. was founded in 1925 and is headquartered in Juno Beach, Florida.
